integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic surreal body horror, photorealistic. <Subject 1> stands facing the camera in a tiled changing room at a public swimming pool, framed from the knees up, fully human and naturally proportioned. The camera pushes in at slow speed. A perfectly straight crease forms diagonally from one shoulder to the opposite hip, and the body bends inward along it like thick living paper: the two sides rotate toward each other in one smooth, controlled movement, and the chest becomes flatter while keeping its human surface. A second crease forms across the abdomen, and the waist becomes a clean geometric hinge while <Subject 1> stays balanced and upright. One forearm flattens from wrist to elbow into a broad thin plane; the hand follows, fingers arranging themselves along the same flat surface. <Subject 1> raises the arm and studies it, and a new fold forms naturally at the elbow. The head stays fully three-dimensional above the folded architecture. In the final moment <Subject 1> turns sideways, and in profile the folded body is only a few centimetres thick.

overall_soundscape: Quiet room ambience, restrained breathing, soft dry folding sounds, and crisp paper tension each time a plane settles.
